{{Use mdy dates|date=October 2024}}
'''Marjorie''' "'''Molly'''" '''Greene Hahn''' (born December 30, 1948) is an American [[mathematician]] and [[tennis]] player. In mathematics and [[mathematical statistics]] she is known for her research in [[probability theory]], including work on [[central limit theorem]]s, [[stochastic process]]es, and [[stochastic differential equation]]s. She is a professor emeritus of mathematics at [[Tufts University]].{{r|res}}

==Education==
Molly Greene did her undergraduate studies at [[Stanford University]], graduating in 1971.{{r|res}} She went on to graduate study at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], and married Peter Florin Hahn in 1973. Like Greene, Peter Hahn had graduated with great distinction from Stanford in 1971;{{r|stangrad}} he was a graduate student in mathematics at [[Harvard University]],{{r|mgp2}} and went on to a career in [[radiology]] at Harvard.{{r|catalyst}}

Marjorie Hahn completed her Ph.D. in 1975. Her dissertation, supervised by [[Richard M. Dudley]], was ''Central Limit Theorems for D[0,1]-Valued Random Variables''.{{r|res|mgp}}

==Academic career==
After postdoctoral study at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], Hahn became a faculty member at [[Tufts University]] in 1977.{{r|res}} While active at Tufts, she supervised the dissertations of 16 doctoral students, more than anyone else in the department;{{r|res|mgp}} her students included legal statistician [[Weiwen Miao]].{{r|mgp}} She retired as professor emeritus in 2016.{{r|res|tuftsnow}}

In 1985, Hahn was elected as a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].{{r|res|fims}}

==Tennis==
Hahn is also a [[tennis]] player. She played on the [[Stanford Cardinals]] team from 1967 to 1971,{{r|amc2}} and passed up a chance to play tennis professionally in favor of her work in mathematics.{{r|res}} In 2006, her name was added to the United States Tennis Association New England Hall of Fame.{{r|res}}

In 2008, she represented the U.S. in an international seniors competition, the Alice Marble Cup,{{r|amc2|amc}} where she helped her team win a silver medal.{{r|amc2}} In 2017, she was part of a U.S. team that won the Kitty Godfrey Cup for women 65 or over at the [[International Tennis Federation]] World Super-Senior team championships.{{r|kgc}}

Comparing mathematics with tennis, Hahn has said "In mathematics, you try to prove things step by step; you attempt to set up a logical method. I approach tennis by using this plan and then adjust on the fly."{{r|amc}}
